Available in: English Français Español 日本語 简体中文 한국어 Português 繁體中文 The stream of a lifetime. A broadcaster breaking news. A million-euro deal that just can’t wait. There are moments that matter, and moments that matter more. This is what differentiated connectivity is all about. Let's explore how you can make the most of these moments. This is your moment There are critical moments in consumers' and businesses’ daily lives when network performance matter more, and when willingness to pay surges – whether they’re streaming live video from a concert, managing secure mobile payments at a bustling festival, or engaging in a pivotal online gaming session. These are moments when differentiated connectivity truly makes a difference. Differentiated connectivity is about creating service offerings with predictable performance that meets the diverse requirements of both consumer and enterprise applications. Bringing differentiated connectivity to life So many choices, such high stakes. A visualization of the options makes the decisions easier, and the deal can be closed. A flow moment: With 5G enabled headsets connected to the company cloud, the customers can visualize different options and make joint, assured decisions for their purchase. Connected to the cloud, each retail outlet always has access to the latest updates. What if you could offer retail chains a 5G package with guaranteed performance that ensures consistent immersive experience across the retail locations. Time is critical. The delivery can’t be late. Drones can take direct routes through urban environments. The flow moment: Rapid response drones help critical resources and support reach the scene faster or improve situational awareness. What if you could offer a package with predictable and secure network performance and capabilities for delivery drones enabling new mission-critical services when every second counts. Total blackout. Your job is to fix it. Handsfree access to intelligence changes the game. The flow moment: A field technician is expected to resolve problems quickly and efficiently. With AR smart glasses connected to AI, all information is available instantly enabling handsfree working with intelligent assistance. What if you could offer a package enabling first time right outcomes to companies with field technicians, utilising superior uplink with millisecond latency for video AI assistants. The big game is on. Excitement is in the air. The security staff keeps one step ahead and makes sure everyone is safe A flow moment: The stadium is filling up. The event security operations center has full situational awareness. Video streams feeds information from body cams, fixed cameras and drones. The security staff can be directed to always be at the right place at the right time. What if you offered a secure, dedicated connection for situational awareness so that the event security operations team can take better informed decisions. Broadcasting that once-in-a-lifetime event There are big moments that need sharing to an expectant audience. The ‘Flow’ moment. A spectacular sight needs capturing and sharing to millions while on location. Differentiated connectivity allows you to deliver guaranteed uplink for seamless live broadcasting. What if you offered a performance-based connection for media companies to keep their audiences watching and entertained. In the high paced world of news and media, to be first makes all the difference. Competition is fierce A Done moment: The photojournalist that captures that great shot needs to get it to publishers instantly. This is what will make or break the day – or even the career - for the photographer. The file is big is and precious. What if you offered a package guaranteeing accelerated upload speeds when it is needed to give the photographer a competitive advantage. 1000s of excited fans are waiting online for the live stream. Special guests are joining, multiplying the fan base. Pre-promotion has been great. The stream must be perfect. What if you could offer a package where influencers and media can pre-book guaranteed uplink at a certain time at certain place. Your favorite team is playing. It is a make-or-break game Match days are the best days and this is a must win game. You have been looking forward to this. You have secured tickets for really good seats. You want to be able to share the excitement and enrich the game experience with access to instant replays at critical moments, like VAR decisions. What if you offered a package for dedicated fans, that gives both downlink and uplink speeds, to watch replays, get player stats and share the magic moments with friends that could not come. The big screen for the big game. Streams surge. And at the same time family life goes on with business meetings, gaming and browsing. The flow moment: The home network stands up to deliver a premium experience for all family members connected at once. What if you offered a premium FWA package this summer to secure great sports experiences from the sofa, while the rest of the home stays online without compromise. Flawless payments ‘flow’ at the big match With 190 million card payments each day in Europe alone, differentiated connectivity ensures your payment terminals stay cool under pressure. The ‘Flow’ Moment. The big game has arrived and you’re a food truck vendor at a stadium with 60,000 fans. Making the most of the opportunity to sell as much food as you can! With a secure, dedicated connection to make sure transactions go through, its going to be a very profitable day. What if you created a proposition for small businesses where they could have this service wherever (and whenever) they needed to take payment. Keeping their customers happy and products flying off the shelf. Today we want to work efficiently anywhere and at any time, with access to files and resources just as in the office. A win moment: The team is on their way to a critical customer meeting. The presentation must be updated with the latest figures. Collaborating on the necessary edits and getting the information from the company servers they will be able to get ready before arrival. What if you could offer a package with predictable and secure cloud connection, so enterprises can enable employees to be productive on the move? Help secure the next big deal moment Not all business moments are equal. Some need reliable connectivity at the right time. The ‘Win moment’. A high-stakes video call for the deal of the century and you’re stuck in traffic. A deal that won’t wait. Differentiated connectivity deliver a secure, dedicated connection for uninterrupted conferencing. What if you offered a performance-based proposition dedicated for executives, so they can connect with their customer and secure the big deal. Capturing the ‘wow’ moment at the big concert To stay relevant with thousands of followers, differentiated connectivity ensures influencers connect and stream without lag regardless of the network traffic generated by thousands of fans at major events. The ‘Wow’ moment. The big concert. Thousands of fans in one venue. Right in the middle of it all, an influencer is livestreaming the entire experience. With a dedicated network slice and superior uplink performance, they can stream in the most crowded environments, no buffering, no lag — just seamless, real-time sharing. What if you created a performance-based proposition dedicated for influencers and content creators, so they can entertain their followers and raise their profile to attract new audiences. Take the ‘win’ moment to the next level To be in the moment, differentiated connectivity ensures gamers stay connected on the move without lag and buffering. The ‘Win’ moment. The crucial game. Being part of the team. Right in the middle of a big level, a gamer is in the thick of the action. With super low ping and millisecond latency, they can reach the final round — just seamless, real-time moments to stay competitive without a worry of letting everyone down. What if you created a performance-based proposition dedicated for gamers, so they can stay in the moment, complete their challenge, and get to the next level. 5G Talks 5G Standalone: A winning strategy for business growth Ericsson experts and telco operators MasOrange and Telia discuss how 5G Standalone and differentiated connectivity can support new commercial models, stronger customer experiences, long-term competitiveness and enhanced brand equity. MasOrange reveal insights into their differentiated connectivity journey. Angelica Sanchez, Brand Portfolio Director and Alberto Pérez Velasco, Value Proposition Manager, share their challenges, learnings and top takeaways from investing in 5G Standalone and the creation of new offers for their customers. Watch the full 5G Talks broadcast. Gain valuable insights from new global research on differentiated connectivity and its business impact Hear how leading providers MasOrange and Telia are testing and launching new propositions Understand what growing AI usage means for future network demands Discover where real opportunities for growth are emerging and how performance is central to success Moments in action Today, nearly all mobile service offerings are centered around packages of data volume. These offerings are delivered with “best-effort” performance, giving users the best possible performance the network can currently deliver. The challenge is that the connection isn't guaranteed at the specific moment the user needs it most. Differentiated connectivity provides CSPs with the opportunity to explore and consider performance as a value proposition, expanding new types of tiered and premium service offerings to consumers and enterprises. Here’s a few examples: From best-effort to best-in-class connectivity — premium FWA in remote areas of Greece COSMOTE TELEKOM is redefining connectivity in Greece — bringing high-quality broadband to islands and mountain communities where traditional fiber rollout simply isn't feasible. As the first provider in the country to fully leverage Fixed Wireless Access on a 5G Standalone network, powered by Ericsson, they are setting a new standard for what advanced connectivity can look like. 5G Standalone for autonomous transport Telia and Ericsson are collaborating with global truck manufacturer Scania to explore how Ericsson’s 5G Standalone capabilities, delivered through Telia’s network, can provide the predictable performance autonomous operations require at scale. This is part of the NorthStar innovation program launched by Telia and Ericsson. Singtel's journey into differentiated connectivity Explore the case study to gain insights from Singtel's innovative stepwise journey into differentiated connectivity: exploration, scale, and commercialization. Festival vendors get superior connectivity Working with Vodafone, we had dedicated connectivity for food and drink vendors and event operations teams at a festival in the UK. Insight to help with your business case Insights driving moments that matter Moments of hope, desire or unease make peoples’ willingness to pay suddenly skyrocket. These moments represent an opportunity for the telecom industry to bring new offerings to the market and drive growth. In this article series, we explain and demonstrate how. A new opportunity for the telecom industry: Introducing moments – when willingness to pay spikes. Read insight series: part 1 Get to know the four types of moments Read insight series: part 2 Turn planned moments into offerings – Wow! and Flow! Read insight series: part 3 Turn spontaneous moments into offerings – Done! and Win! Read insight series: part 4 Scale up with moments – from unique offerings to a portfolio of moments Read insight series: part 5 An agentic life: How AI use reshapes user expectations ConsumerLab’s new report explores how three trends in AI use are changing user behavior and creating new market opportunities in telecom. Differentiated connectivity entering the market at speed Ericsson Mobility Report: The number of commercially available offerings based on 5G standalone (SA) network slicing has surged to 84 – a significant jump from the 65 reported just 6 months ago – signaling that differentiated connectivity is rapidly moving from early adoption to mainstream commercialization. Winning in the market with differentiated connectivity Differentiated connectivity can elevate key moments for 5G users. Our Ericsson ConsumerLab report ‘Winning in the market with differentiated connectivity offerings’ provides consumer behavior insights related to their experiences and expectations of mobile services and explores the opportunities that opens up for service providers. Scale your portfolio of premium offerings at events Large sporting events and huge concerts drive large numbers of visitors to towns, cities and venues. For fans, a premium connection elevates their experience. For the ecosystem of partners and businesses, having a predicable network connection that supports their business outcomes is crucial. Developing propositions to support fans and businesses and organizations generates new revenue opportunities for mobile operators. What do you need to make this happen? How do you achieve differentiated connectivity? It’s a journey that unlocks your network potential. Access our handbook that will take you through our three-stage blueprint of exploration, scaling and monetization – designed to help you craft a competitive edge. Explore how Differentiated connectivity: turning the network into a revenue engine In this conversation, Cecilia Atterwall, Head of Group Marketing, and Patrick Johansson, SVP and Head of Market Area Europe, Middle East and Africa, explore how communications service providers can turn 5G investments into differentiated value and new revenue streams. The focus shifts from Megabits per second to outcomes: a video call that never fails, a stadium experience that just works, or enterprise connectivity with assured performance. The technical foundation is 5G Standalone with network slicing and SLAs that enable guaranteed performance when and where it matters. Looking for more information on differentiated connectivity? Discover how our story evolved; from manufacturing some of the first telephones to managing networks that process 40% of the world's data. Explore our history 2024: Internet of Things - and more! For long now, Ericsson has been dedicated to advancing 5G, enabling the Internet of Things. Presently, Ericsson is also engaged in the development of 6G, anticipating that it will deliver an “extended reality” experience, engaging all our senses. 1991: GSM changes everything After NMT (1G) came GSM (2G), enabling even more widespread use of mobile telephony. On July 1, 1991, the new European GSM standard was introduced across many European countries, with GSM calls being made in Germany, Finland, Denmark, and Sweden over Ericsson systems. 1976: The AXE-switch The days of analog switches were coming to an end. New electronic and digital systems would replace them – and so Ericsson built the AXE switching system, as a joint venture with Swedish PTT Televerket. AXE was revolutionary in several ways, particularly through its advanced modular system architecture – and Ericsson would prosper with it for many decades to come. 1956: Mobile telephony awakens Ericsson's very first mobile phone, designed in 1956, weighed like a young teenager at 40 kilos and was about the size of a suitcase. Perhaps not really “mobile”. And never destined to be a best-seller, since the network that was built to support it couldn’t handle more than 100 subscribers. (In 1987 that Ericsson would release its first real handheld mobile phone, the HotLine Pocket.) 1923: 500-switch When it arrived, the 500-switch automatic telephone system was a mechanical marvel, capable of handling a whopping 500 lines. The first Ericsson 500-switch station was put in operation in 1923. Eight years later, Ericsson had delivered about 100 stations with a total of more than 350,000 lines. Sales continued to increase over several decades. By 1974, when sales eventually started to decline, 4.8 million lines using the 500-switch were in operation in public telephone stations. 1876: Lars Magnus Ericsson starts a mechanical workshop In 1876 Lars Magnus Ericsson started a small mechanical workshop in central Stockholm, which went on to become one of the world’s leading information and communication technology companies. In 1880, he launched the first wall-mounted telephone and delivered the first switchboard.
